takeaway: The adductor canal carries the femoral artery and vein, saphenous nerve and nerve to vastus medialis; adductor longus is supplied by the obturator nerve, which stays outside.

question.text: Which of the following structures does not enter the adductor canal?

lines.text: The adductor canal runs from the apex of the femoral triangle to the adductor hiatus.
Inside, the femoral artery and vein walk through together.
With them travel the saphenous nerve and the nerve to vastus medialis.
At the hiatus, the vessels enter the popliteal fossa as the popliteal artery and vein.
But the nerve to adductor longus is stopped at the door.
lines.say: (laugh) But the nerve to adductor longus is stopped at the door.

lines.text: Adductor longus is supplied by the obturator nerve, which does not travel in the canal.
So the nerve to adductor longus does not enter the adductor canal.
